source_caption:
Some movies break your heart in the simplest way possible. 💔

Hachi: A Dog’s Tale (2009) tells the story of a dog whose love for his owner never fades, even when life takes a turn neither of them could have imagined.

Every day, Hachi waits at the train station for Parker to return home. What begins as a small daily routine becomes something much deeper — a reminder of what it means to love someone without expecting anything in return.

Based on the true story of Hachikō, a Japanese Akita who continued waiting for his deceased owner at a train station for nearly ten years, the film shows just how powerful the bond between a human and a dog can be.

Sometimes, the purest love comes from a creature that can’t say a single word.

And if you’ve ever loved a dog, you already know why this movie hurts so much.

source_details.synopsis: Hachi: A Dog's Tale is a 2009 drama film and a remake of Seijirō Kōyama's 1987 Japanese film Hachikō Monogatari. The original film told the true story of the Akita dog named Hachikō who lived in Japan 1923–1935. Hachi: A Dog's Tale is an updated American adaptation based on the Japanese film. This version, which places it in a modern American context, was directed by Lasse Hallström, written by Stephen P. Lindsey and Kaneto Shindo, and produced by Richard Gere, Bill Johnson and Vicki Shigekuni Wong. The film stars Gere, Joan Allen, Sarah Roemer, Jason Alexander, and Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa.
